title: Find Latest Group of Size M
statement:
Let `n` be the length of `arr`, which holds each number from `1` to `n` exactly once. Start from a row of `n` bits, all `0`, numbered `1` to `n`. The process runs for `n` steps: at step `i` (counting from `1`), the bit numbered `arr[i - 1]` becomes `1`.

A **group** is a run of consecutive `1` bits that is maximal: the bit just before it and the bit just after it are `0` or do not exist.

Return the largest step number after which some group has length exactly `m`. If that never happens at any step, return `-1`.
constraints: All values in arr are distinct
notes:
## Intuition

The direct way rebuilds the bit row after every step and measures all of its runs, which is O(n²). But a step changes very little: the new `1` either stands alone, extends one neighbouring group, or joins the two groups on its sides into one. If we know the length of the group touching each side, and how many groups currently have each length, one step costs O(1), and "is there a group of length `m` right now?" is just `count[m] > 0`.

## Approach

1. Keep `length`, indexed by bit position with a spare `0` at both ends: for every group, the entries at its two end positions hold its length.
2. Keep `count[len]`, the number of groups of length `len` right now.
3. At each step, read `leftLength` from the position just left of `position` and `rightLength` from the position just right of it. A `0` bit there gives `0`.
4. The new group has `merged = leftLength + rightLength + 1` bits. Write it at its two ends, `position - leftLength` and `position + rightLength`.
5. The two old groups disappear and the new one appears, so update `count` accordingly.
6. If `count[m] > 0`, record this step in `latest`. Return `latest` at the end.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr = [3, 5, 1, 2, 4]`, `m = 1`. Steps 1–3 place isolated bits at 3, 5 and 1, each a group of length 1, so `count[1]` reaches `3` and `latest = 3`. Step 4 places bit 2: `leftLength = 1` and `rightLength = 1`, so `merged = 3`; `count[1]` drops to `1` (bit 5 is still alone), so `latest = 4`. Step 5 places bit 4 between groups of lengths 3 and 1, making one group of 5; `count[1]` becomes `0`. The answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each step does a constant amount of work.
- Space: O(n) for `length` and `count`.

## Pitfalls

- Only a group's two end positions are kept up to date; inner positions may hold stale lengths, but no new bit is ever placed next to an inner position.
- Pad `length` with a slot at index `0` and `n + 1` so the neighbours of positions `1` and `n` read as `0` without bounds checks.
- Check `count[m]` after every step, not only when a group of length `m` is created: a step can also keep an older such group alive.
- `count[0]` goes negative when a side is empty; it is never read because `m >= 1`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `length` | group length stored at each group's end positions |
| `count` | how many groups currently have each length |
| `latest` | the last step that had a group of length `m` |
| `step` | 0-based index into `arr` (the step number minus one) |
| `position` | the bit turned on in this step |
| `leftLength`, `rightLength` | lengths of the groups touching `position` on each side |
| `merged` | length of the group that `position` now belongs to |

narration.3: length[p] holds the length of the group that ends at position p; the extra slots at 0 and n + 1 stay 0.
narration.4: count[len] says how many groups of length len exist right now.
narration.5: No step has had a group of length m yet.

narration.9: The group ending just left of it (or 0 if that bit is off)...
narration.10: ...and the group starting just right of it.
narration.11: The new bit glues both neighbours into one group.
narration.12: Store the new length at the group's left end...
narration.13: ...and at its right end, the only places a later step will read.
narration.14: The left neighbour group no longer exists on its own.
narration.15: Neither does the right neighbour group.
narration.16: One new group of the merged length now exists.
narration.17: Is there a group of length exactly m after this step?
narration.18: Then this step is the latest one so far.
narration.21: Return the last step that had such a group, or -1.
